case_name: United States v. Ahold U.S.A., Inc. and Peapod LLC (DOJ Settlement)
court: DOJ settlement agreement — no civil docket (administrative enforcement)
defendant_name: Peapod LLC / Ahold U.S.A., Inc. (online grocery delivery)
claim_type: Online grocery delivery website (Peapod.com) and mobile app inaccessible to blind, deaf, and users with physical disabilities
outcome: DOJ settlement — Peapod must conform website and app to WCAG 2.0 AA; designate Web Accessibility Coordinator; adopt accessibility policy; conduct annual user testing; retain independent consultant
estimated_defense_cost: Not disclosed; remediation costs for full WCAG 2.0 overhaul of grocery platform significant

sources.name: DOJ — Justice Department enters settlement agreement with Peapod (Nov 17, 2014)
Seyfarth Shaw — DOJ enters into another website accessibility agreement (2014)

summary_one_line: DOJ required an online-only grocery delivery business to achieve full WCAG 2.0 AA compliance across its website and mobile app — establishing DOJ's enforcement framework for digital accessibility.
notes: November 17, 2014. Part of DOJ's broader push on website accessibility before formal rulemaking. The settlement's requirements (Web Accessibility Coordinator, policy adoption, annual user testing, independent consultant) became a template for subsequent DOJ settlements. No monetary penalty disclosed — the cost is the compliance program.
